title: At-Tawwab, the Ever-Relenting
hook: the Ever-Relenting, who turns toward those who turn
tomorrow: if He turns to all who turn, what about wrongs never made right?

segments.voice: A week of Names, back for one more look. Al-Akhir, last. Az-Zahir, manifest. Al-Batin, hidden. Al-Wali, he governs. Al-Muta'ali, exalted. And yesterday, Al-Barr: goodness. Today's Name is the one you need when goodness slipped.
screen: `LAST · MANIFEST · HIDDEN.` → `HE GOVERNS · EXALTED · GOODNESS.` → `AND WHEN GOODNESS SLIPS?`

segments.voice: A text sits in drafts for days. Two words: i'm sorry. Every hour it waits, it gets harder to send, because now it isn't only sorry for the thing. It's sorry for the wait. Yesterday's question was whether the door still opens if you turn back late. Today's Name is the answer, and it's built for exactly this.
screen: `TWO WORDS IN DRAFTS.` → `SORRY FOR THE WAIT, TOO.` → `DOES THE DOOR STILL OPEN?`

segments.voice: At-Tawwab, the Ever-Relenting. Tawba, in Arabic, means turning back, and At-Tawwab is the One who turns toward whoever turns, and keeps doing it. The Qur'an tells it from the very beginning, after Adam's slip, in Pickthall's words: "Then Adam received from his Lord words (of revelation), and He relented toward him." On the late part, a hadith in Tirmidhi says God accepts a servant's turning until the last breath. Late isn't locked. And the welcome isn't cold. In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, tells of a man in the desert whose camel wanders off with his food and water. He gives up and lies down to wait for death. He wakes, and it's standing right there. God, the Prophet says, is more pleased with a servant's turning than that man with his camel. That's the one to tell a friend tonight. Now watch this week's Names fold into it. The Last, still there at the end of the day. The Outward and the Hidden, near enough to hear a whisper of sorry. The Governor, the Exalted, the Source of Goodness. And At-Tawwab, turning toward the one who turns.
screen: `TAWBA: TURNING BACK.` · `ADAM, TURNED TOWARD.` · `UNTIL THE LAST BREATH.` · `THE LOST CAMEL, FOUND.` · then, large: `HE TURNS TO ME.`

segments.voice: Write one short line by hand: something you'd like to turn back from, or someone you'd like to turn back toward. Keep it private. For the sit, just hold the line, and the open door it's facing.
screen: `ONE LINE, BY HAND.` · `FACING AN OPEN DOOR.`

segments.voice: At-Tawwab. The Ever-Relenting: the One who turns toward those who turn, even late, and is glad when they do.
Your line: he turns to me, every time i turn. Two weeks of Names, and the door's still open.

howItsDone: Muslims make tawba by stopping a wrong, regretting it and resolving not to return to it, and, where someone was wronged, by making it right with them; they call on Allah as ya Tawwab in du'a.

fork.setup: your little brother broke your headphones, hid it for a week, and finally confesses. what would At-Tawwab suggest you do first?
options: turn toward him: the door stays open for someone who turns, even late.
make him wait a week too, so it all feels fair.

fork.reveal: At-Tawwab turns toward whoever turns, late included, and is glad. people aren't God, but the Name gives a direction to lean.
